claims.value: Bodart: side A (French and allies) 14,000 besiegers under Reille and 11,000 covering troops under Saint-Cyr, total 25,000; side B (Spanish) 3,500 garrison.
claims.rationale: Available-for-engagement figures under Bodart’s rounded-up convention (shared research-conventions index), unless the entry specifies a surrender population. claims.value: Saint-Cyr records Reille charged with the siege and completing the investment on 7 November; Reille and Pino were before Rosas, Souham at La Junquera.
claims.rationale: Local besieging command within Saint-Cyr’s superior operation; covering and besieging forces are not interchangeable. English rendering (ours): "Reille and Pino’s divisions camped before Roses, Souham at La Junquera; on the 7th Reille, charged with the siege, completed the investment."

claims.value: Side B held a citadel and Trinidad fort, repaired entrenchments and cut street-mouth trenches.
claims.rationale: Permanent works are inherited; responsibility and phase of the repairs remain unresolved. English rendering (ours): "Its main fortress was the citadel; the star-shaped Trinidad fort stood nearby; the damaged entrenchment was partly repaired and street mouths cut with trenches."

claims.value: Saint-Cyr’s transition calls 7 December the day after the capture of Rosas, implying 6 December; this differs from the frozen 5 December end date.
claims.rationale: Source-specific date implication retained without correcting the frozen frame or treating departure as surrender. English rendering (ours): "The day after the capture of Roses, 7 December, troops left their positions around the place."
